title: 77 K superconducting REBCO interposer frees HBM from beachfront
idea: Extreme user: MRI and fusion-magnet labs that run HTS tape at 77 K. Pattern REBCO thin-film transmission lines on a sapphire/MgO interposer held at 77 K by a closed-cycle cooler; lossless, near-dispersion-free lines let 16-32 HBM-class stacks sit 5-20 cm from the GPU instead of crowding its edge, with no retimers or equalizers.
why: Breaks the shoreline/beachfront limit (~8 stacks per GPU) and the interposer reticle limit; 2-4x memory capacity per accelerator at similar pJ/bit; generalizes to any cryo-cooled AI rack.

title: Downhole micro-Dewar layer lets DRAM sit directly atop hot GPUs
idea: Downhole logging tools survive 200 C by putting electronics in vacuum flasks. Insert a vacuum-gap/silica-aerogel interlayer between logic and a DRAM stack, crossed only by sparse hybrid-bonded copper pillars for signals, and give the DRAM its own top-side cold plate, so memory stays below 70 C while logic runs at 105 C.
why: Enables memory-on-logic 3D stacking (no interposer, mm-to-um wires, ~5-10x lower I/O energy) without the refresh doubling and retention loss that hit DRAM above 85 C.

title: Irvine-style edge-metallized die cubes replace TSVs in memory stacks
idea: 1990s military/space 'cube' memories laminated thinned dies and wired them along a ground, metallized side face. Stack 16-32 thinned DRAM dies with edge-routed RDL fans, polish and metallize the cube face at ~10 um pitch, then turn the cube on its side and hybrid-bond that face to a logic base die or interposer.
why: Eliminates TSV keep-out area, TSV etch/fill tools and TSV yield loss (behind HBM's ~3x area per bit and 20-30% yield hit); dies can be near-standard DDR dies with an edge RDL.

title: Mars-rover microspring sockets make HBM stacks field-replaceable
idea: Planetary hardware survives -120/+20 C cycling with compliant interconnect. Attach each HBM stack to the interposer through lithographic MEMS microsprings at 20-40 um pitch, clamped by a frame lid instead of soldered microbumps, so a stack that fails final test or dies in the field is swapped rather than scrapping the GPU module.
why: Attacks the compounded HBM/CoWoS yield tax (20-30%): one bad stack no longer kills $20-40k of silicon; memory can also be upgraded or reused across GPU generations.

title: Display-fab chip-on-glass panels as giant memory interposers
idea: Display driver ICs are bonded to glass with anisotropic conductive film for pennies per chip. Use depreciated Gen-6/8.5 LCD lines to pattern 2 um Cu RDL on glass panels, then bond DRAM and logic chiplets with fine-pitch ACF or microbumps, making half-meter interposers that hold dozens of memory stacks.
why: Bypasses the CoWoS silicon-interposer chokepoint and its reticle limit; panel cost per mm2 ~10-20x below silicon and uses idle display capacity plus US glass makers.

title: Uncut wafer-scale DRAM plane with stitched redundancy routing
idea: Wafer-scale engines built for national labs never dice. Leave a DRAM wafer whole, add a stitched cross-reticle RDL mesh, laser-fuse out bad dies and route around them, then face-bond it to a wafer of logic tiles or use it as a 1-2 TB memory board with on-wafer wiring.
why: Removes dicing, per-die packaging and handling (~15-25% of back-end cost) and gives terabyte-scale memory over on-wafer links at ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit instead of board traces.

title: Append-only log port built for KV-cache streaming
idea: The long-context KV cache is an extreme user: written once per token, appended sequentially, read whole every step. Add a port mode with a hardware append pointer (writes carry no address) and descriptor-driven sequential read streams, so command/address traffic, row-conflict scheduling and refresh collisions largely vanish for that region.
why: Cuts CA pins ~60% and lifts bus efficiency from ~70% to ~95% for KV traffic; ~30% more bandwidth per pin without new cells.

title: EV-pack style series voltage stacking of HBM dies
idea: EV battery packs put cells in series to cut current. Wire the 12-16 dies of a memory stack as four series voltage domains (e.g., 4.4 V across four 1.1 V groups), with on-die switched-capacitor balancers absorbing activity mismatch, so the stack draws a quarter of the current.
why: Power/ground TSVs and bumps, a large share of HBM's TSV budget, drop ~4x and IR drop shrinks, freeing area for signals or taller stacks; eases the TSV tax and base-die PDN area.

title: Radio-telescope corner-turn base die gives free transposes
idea: Radio correlators (SKA, ALMA) spend much of their memory budget on the 'corner turn' that transposes time-major data to frequency-major. Store tiles diagonally skewed across banks and add a butterfly transpose network in the HBM base die, so a matrix written row-major streams out column-major at full burst efficiency.
why: Strided/transposed reads waste 50-90% of fetched bytes (page overfetch); attention, FFT and weight-gradient transposes run at full efficiency, ~2-5x effective bandwidth in those phases.

title: Climate-model halo links: memory stacks talk directly to neighbors
idea: Weather codes are dominated by halo exchange between neighboring domains. Add short serial side-links from each HBM base die to the nearest stack of the adjacent GPU, so halos, KV pages and pipeline activations migrate memory-to-memory without crossing either GPU's PHY and NoC.
why: Halves PHY crossings for inter-GPU transfers (each ~1-5 pJ/bit) and frees GPU I/O for compute traffic; lets neighboring GPUs pool capacity instead of duplicating it.

title: Stadium-broadcast optical star coupler shares weights across 64 accelerators
idea: Broadcast TV sends one stream to millions of receivers. Keep one copy of model weights in a shared memory appliance whose optical output is split by a passive star coupler to 64 accelerators at once; each GPU's HBM holds only KV cache and activations while layers stream in lockstep.
why: Inference clusters store identical weights in every GPU's HBM; broadcasting removes 30-60% of per-GPU HBM capacity demand, directly stretching scarce HBM supply.

title: Genlock-synchronized command-free memory interface
idea: Broadcast studios genlock every device to one reference so nothing negotiates timing. The compiler emits a static access schedule for a training step; host and memory base die run identical cycle-accurate sequencers locked to a shared clock, so no commands or addresses cross the interface, only data and a rare resync word.
why: Repurposes CA pins as data (+20-30% bandwidth per pin), removes controller complexity and makes row-hammer-safe schedules provable at compile time.

title: ROADM-style wavelength-addressed DRAM banks
idea: Telecom ROADMs route by color, not by address decode. Give each bank group a microring drop filter tuned to its own wavelength; the host picks the target bank by choosing a comb-laser line, so light itself routes the request and data to the bank and the global electrical decode and data bus disappear.
why: Attacks periphery (~49% of die) and global-wire energy; bank parallelism scales with comb lines (16-64) rather than with wires.

title: Aircraft wireless-avionics bus inside the package cavity
idea: Airliners adopt wireless avionics intra-communication to delete harness weight. Give each chiplet a 300 GHz on-die antenna radiating into the metal-lidded package cavity, which acts as a shared multimode waveguide; frequency channels replace interposer traces, so memory chiplets can sit anywhere on a cheap organic substrate.
why: Removes dependence on silicon interposers/bridges (CoWoS chokepoint) and on beachfront geometry; any-to-any memory sharing among chiplets.

title: Implant body-channel trick: send memory data over power planes
idea: Implants use the body itself as the wire (intra-body communication). Superimpose low-amplitude multi-GHz carriers on the stack's power/ground TSV network and separate them on each die with on-die band-pass filters, so power TSVs double as data channels.
why: Power and ground take a large share of HBM TSVs and bumps; reusing them adds ~1.5-2x signal capacity without more TSVs, easing the TSV tax.

title: Phone-PMIC embedded die: DRAM inside the substrate under GPU
idea: Phones embed PMICs and passives inside the PCB core to save height. Embed thinned DRAM dies in cavities of the accelerator's organic substrate directly beneath the GPU, connected by laser-drilled microvias to the GPU's bottom bumps.
why: Memory moves from the beachfront to under the die (~200 um wires) with no silicon interposer; frees GPU perimeter and sidesteps CoWoS capacity limits.

title: GaN-on-diamond radar trick: diamond interlayers enable 32-high stacks
idea: Military radars bond GaN to CVD diamond to dump extreme heat flux. Insert 20-50 um CVD-diamond spreader layers every four DRAM dies, with laser-cut windows for TSVs, carrying heat sideways to a side-wall cold plate.
why: Thermal resistance caps HBM at ~12-16 high; diamond (~2000 W/mK, lab-grown in the US) allows ~32-high stacks, ~2x bits per footprint without denser cells.

title: Industrial-longevity harvest-and-rebin of retired server DRAM
idea: Factories keep 30-year-old controllers alive by harvesting parts. Build automated lines that pull DIMMs from retired servers, burn-in and speed-bin them, and repackage the dies into CXL memory expanders for cold/warm tiers sold with a supply guarantee.
why: Hyperscalers retire servers every 4-6 years with DRAM good for 10+; recovering even 30% adds several percent to annual usable supply at a fraction of new-bit cost.

title: XIP-style narrow serial DRAM chiplets for a bulk capacity tier
idea: $1 microcontrollers execute in place from 12-pin Octal-SPI/HyperRAM parts. Define a 12-16-pin high-speed serial DRAM chiplet for accelerator capacity tiers, ringed on cheap substrate, with a large logic-side cache hiding latency.
why: Pins and PHY area per GB drop ~5-10x vs DDR/HBM, so many cheap older-node DRAM dies add capacity without HBM's TSV and interposer costs.

title: Fly-by-wire redundancy: erasure-code across stacks to accept defective dies
idea: Flight controls tolerate failed channels by redundancy. Stripe each cache line with a Reed-Solomon code across 8+2 stacks/channels, so stacks with dead channels or weak dies can ship and run; the controller remaps on the fly.
why: Turns part of the 20-30% HBM stack yield loss into usable supply; worthwhile when yield loss exceeds the ~20% parity overhead.

title: Stretchable-electronics liquid-metal bumps for warpage-free giant panels
idea: Stretchable wearables connect rigid chips with gallium alloy that never fatigues. Attach memory dies to large glass or organic panels with encapsulated eutectic gallium-indium microbump wells (30-50 um pitch) at room temperature, absorbing CTE mismatch and allowing rework by warming.
why: Warpage and reflow mismatch cap interposer and package size; room-temperature compliant joints allow 100-stack panels and rework, raising assembly yield.

title: Trusted-packaging-first US strategy: stack imported wafers domestically
idea: DoD trusted-foundry users secure supply through trusted assembly. Fund US memory OSATs that buy commodity DRAM wafers from several countries and do base-die integration, stacking, test and HBM/CXL module assembly onshore, with tariff exemptions on wafers and offtake from federal AI programs.
why: Packaging capex is ~1/10 of a DRAM fab with a 1-2 year ramp; moves the highest-value, scarcest step (HBM assembly) onshore years before a US fab could.

title: Qubit-fridge FDM: dozens of memory channels on one trace
idea: Quantum computers frequency-multiplex qubit readout because fridge wires are precious. Carry 16-32 memory channels as QAM subcarriers on one wideband line with integrated mm-wave mixers at both ends, so a far memory module needs a few lines instead of hundreds of pins.
why: Cuts pin, beachfront and routing cost ~10x for capacity tiers, letting memory sit on cheap remote boards; the trade is mixer power.

title: Hearing-aid LC resonant bus recycles line charge
idea: Hearing aids live on a 1-2 mW zinc-air budget. Pair each memory data line with an integrated on-package inductor so line plus inductor form a resonant tank; bits are sent as half-cycles of resonance, so the line's charge sloshes back instead of being dumped to ground each transition.
why: Recovering 80-90% of line CV2 cuts I/O energy ~5-10x; on short HBM-class wires this reaches ~10x lower interface energy per access (fact 5).

title: Deep-space PPM: one pulse carries four to six bits
idea: NASA's deep-space optical link uses pulse-position modulation because photons are scarce. Encode each 4-6-bit symbol as the position of a single short current pulse within a 16-64-slot frame on each memory lane; one transition per symbol replaces several NRZ transitions, and idle lanes send nothing.
why: Transitions per bit fall ~4-8x; with low-swing pulsed drivers, link energy ~10x below DDR5/HBM PHYs, at the cost of a faster slot clock and tighter timing.

title: Cryo-EM style LN2 memory drawer at 0.4 V and 50 mV swing
idea: Cryo-EM and magnet labs already handle LN2 routinely. Immerse whole memory drawers in liquid nitrogen: at 77 K subthreshold swing ~20 mV/dec lets periphery run at ~0.4 V and links at ~50 mV, copper resistance falls ~7x, and access-transistor leakage collapses so refresh nearly stops.
why: CV2 per access ~8-10x lower and refresh (~46 fJ/bit idle) vanishes at the memory; cryocooler overhead (~3-10 W/W) eats much of it, so net only wins with cheap industrial LN2 (~1.5-3x).

title: Quantum-computer SFQ pulse links to a 4 K memory
idea: Quantum computers already run single-flux-quantum logic at 4 K to drive qubits. Build the memory interface and periphery in energy-efficient SFQ, where a bit is one flux quantum (~1e-19 J), paired with a cryogenic DRAM array whose leakage is essentially zero.
why: Interface energy per bit falls 100-1000x and refresh disappears; aimed at cryo AI/quantum hybrids where the 4 K budget is already paid, then cryo datacenter pods.

title: RFID backscatter reads: memory reflects bits instead of driving them
idea: Batteryless RFID tags talk by toggling their antenna load to reflect the reader's carrier. The host drives a continuous carrier onto each read lane; the memory base die returns data by switching a tiny termination impedance between reflect and absorb, and the host's coherent receiver demodulates.
why: Memory-side transmit energy drops ~10-50x (a switch toggle instead of a line driver) and stack heat falls, allowing taller stacks; the host carrier is shared across lanes.

title: Stacked-image-sensor split: DRAM sense amps live on logic wafer
idea: Sony's stacked image sensors keep only pixels on top and put ADCs on a logic wafer below, joined by per-block hybrid bonds. Build a DRAM wafer with only cells and bitlines, and hybrid-bond each subarray's local I/O at ~1 um pitch to sense amps, decoders and datapath on an advanced logic wafer underneath.
why: Removes the DRAM global datapath and off-chip I/O (wires shrink from mm to um) and moves periphery (~49% of die) to efficient logic; ~10x lower energy per access if bond capacitance stays below ~1 fF.

title: Contact-lens monolithic memory tiers grown directly over logic
idea: A smart contact lens must fit a whole system in ~1 mm2, which forces monolithic 3D. Grow low-temperature memory tiers sequentially in the BEOL above logic, linked by 100 nm inter-layer vias at 1e7-1e8 per mm2, so each mat has its own micron-length vertical path to compute at ~0.3 V swing.
why: Micron wires and per-mat parallelism give ~10-30 fJ/bit movement, >10x below HBM; via density ~1e4x TSVs removes the bandwidth/beachfront limit.

title: Endoscope imaging-fiber bundle carries 10,000 slow microLED memory lanes
idea: Medical endoscopes pipe whole images through coherent bundles of ~10k fiber cores. Couple a microLED array on the memory module to a photodiode array on the processor through an imaging fiber bundle, each pixel-lane at ~1-2 Gb/s with no SerDes, DSP or lasers.
why: Off-board memory links at ~0.3-0.5 pJ/bit vs DDR5's 10-20 pJ/bit (>10x), so cheap DRAM can sit meters away in pooled racks; avoids laser and EUV scarcity.

title: Astronomy CCD correlated double sampling enables 20 mV memory links
idea: Astronomical CCDs read single electrons by correlated double sampling, subtracting a reset sample from the signal sample. Put clocked CDS receivers on interposer/TSV links so offsets and low-frequency noise cancel, allowing 20-30 mV swings driven from a dedicated switched-capacitor 0.1 V rail.
why: Line energy ~C*Vswing*Vrail: 30 mV swing from a 0.1 V rail vs 0.4 V links cuts wire energy >10x, attacking data-movement energy and the voltage floor at the interface.

title: Neural-implant address-event bus for sparse tensors
idea: Neural implants with 1,000+ electrodes send spikes as address events, not frames, to stay within milliwatts. Store activations and KV in a sparse layout and run the link in address-event representation: only nonzero values with compressed coordinates cross the PHY, each event gating its own lane.
why: At 70-95% activation sparsity (ReLU, MoE, pruned models) bits moved per logical access fall ~3-10x; energy tracks information rather than tensor size.

title: Million-token agents: attention scoring inside the HBM base die
idea: Million-token agent contexts make decode almost pure KV reads. The base die streams keys internally at full TSV bandwidth, computes low-precision q.k scores, and returns only the top-k keys' values plus a residual over the PHY.
why: For long contexts only ~1-5% of values need to cross the interface; PHY energy per logical token access drops 10-20x and HBM bandwidth stops bounding decode.

title: Search-engine Bloom filter skips DRAM row activations
idea: Web search engines consult tiny Bloom filters before touching shards. Keep compact locality-sensitive-hash signatures of KV pages and embedding rows in logic-side SRAM; the controller activates a DRAM row only when its signature predicts relevance, so most rows are never opened.
why: Row activation is a third or more of access energy; skipping ~90% of activations in retrieval, attention and recsys gives ~10x lower energy per useful access with no memory-side change.

title: Progressive-JPEG bit-plane memory: fetch only needed precision
idea: Satellite and web imagery stream progressive bit planes so receivers stop when good enough. Store tensors bit-plane-sliced across columns (sign/exponent plane first, then mantissa planes); each read requests only the top N planes and only those columns are sensed and sent.
why: Most inference reads need 2-4 effective bits of a 16-bit value; energy per access scales with planes fetched, ~4-8x lower, ~10x with shared block exponents.

title: Wake-once sensor: clockless delay-insensitive memory link
idea: Seismic and wildlife sensors that wake once a minute cannot afford PLL/DLL lock power. Replace forwarded clocks, DLLs and link training with a delay-insensitive 1-of-4 code: each 2-bit symbol is one transition on one of four wires plus a completion acknowledge, so energy is spent only per symbol.
why: Clocking, DLLs and idle termination are often half or more of DRAM interface power; removing them plus one transition per two bits cuts energy per access ~5-10x at typical 20-40% utilization.

title: E-paper shelf-label stepwise charging of memory buses
idea: Electronic shelf labels last a decade on a coin cell partly by driving lines in small steps from tank capacitors. Charge each long column-datapath and interposer line through a ladder of N tank-capacitor rails; each step dissipates ~1/N of the CV2 and the tanks recapture charge on discharge.
why: With N=8-10 steps line energy falls ~8-10x, at the cost of ~N-times slower edges, which suits wide-slow buses.

title: MRI-safe metal-free stack: optical vias through silicon at 1310 nm
idea: MRI-compatible implants must avoid metal paths. Silicon is transparent above 1.1 um, so give each die in a stack aligned micro-emitter and germanium photodiode arrays and pass data vertically through the dies as light; only power needs vias.
why: Removes signal TSVs and their capacitance; sub-100 fJ/bit vertical links (~10x below TSV+PHY paths), looser die alignment, and less TSV area tax.

title: Genomics-grade sub-row activation with host column masks
idea: Genome aligners hammer memory with random 8-32-byte k-mer lookups. Add a column-mask field to ACT so segmented local wordline drivers fire only one 512 B segment of a row, and route only those bits to the I/O.
why: Attacks the 128x page overfetch (5.9 pJ per useful random bit): activating 1/16 of a row cuts random-access energy ~8-12x with a small periphery change.

title: Contactless smartcard coupling: unbonded face-to-face capacitive memory links
idea: Contactless smartcards exchange data across air gaps. Place memory and logic dies face-to-face across ~1 um of dielectric with arrays of 5 um capacitor plates, signaling with low-voltage pulses and no metallurgical bond or ESD structures.
why: No ESD, no bumps and ~1-5 fF per channel give ~10-50 fJ/bit (>10x below HBM I/O); dies can be tested and swapped before final assembly, avoiding known-good-die losses.

title: Solar-calculator near-threshold: 100,000 slow lanes at 0.3 V
idea: Solar calculators run for decades at near-threshold voltage by being slow. Use fine-pitch hybrid bonding to give memory 50-100k lanes at only 200-400 Mb/s each, so drivers and receivers run at 0.3 V with no equalization, termination or SerDes.
why: Switching energy scales with V2: 0.3 V lanes vs ~1.1 V I/O give ~13x lower energy at equal aggregate bandwidth; parallelism replaces frequency.

title: Demoscene procedural memory: store generators, regenerate tensors in base die
idea: Demoscene 4 KB intros generate whole worlds from tiny programs. Store weights and KV as compact generators (PRNG seeds, low-rank factors, codebook indices) and expand them in a small base-die engine on read, so the array and interface move only the recipe.
why: Bits stored and moved per logical access fall ~4-16x depending on compressibility, cutting energy per access and multiplying effective capacity.

title: Laptop panel-self-refresh: mirrored dictionaries deduplicate memory link traffic
idea: Laptop eDP panels self-refresh so the GPU stops resending unchanged frames. Keep synchronized small dictionaries of recent 64 B lines at both ends of the memory link; when a line or near-match is already in the far dictionary, send a 10-bit index plus a sparse diff instead of 512 bits.
why: Repeated lines (zero pages, shared prefixes, embeddings) are common; at 50-90% hit rates link energy per access falls ~3-10x without touching cells.

title: Fraud-graph pointer chasing executed inside the memory stack
idea: Fraud-detection and social graphs are extreme pointer chasers with one useful word per hop. Put a tiny walker engine in the base die that follows pointer chains and returns only the final result, keeping every intermediate hop inside the stack.
why: Each hop otherwise crosses the PHY twice with a full burst; internal hops cost far less, ~10x lower energy per logical graph access and lower latency.

title: PON burst-mode PHY: memory links that sleep between bursts
idea: Fiber-to-the-home ONUs transmit in bursts with receivers that lock in tens of ns. Give memory PHYs burst-mode clock-data recovery with short preambles and ~1-5 ns wake, so termination, clocks and CDR are fully off between transactions instead of idling.
why: Memory links average 20-40% utilization yet burn much of their power idle; burst mode makes link energy proportional to accesses, ~5-10x lower energy per access at low utilization.
